questions.text:
Let $A=\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, 9\}$. Let R be a relation on A defined by $(x, y)\in R$ if and only if $|x-y|$ is a multiple of 3.
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $n(R)=36$.
Statement II: R is an equivalence relation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
$(x,y)\in R$ exactly when $x$ and $y$ leave the same remainder on division by 3. The classes are $\{0,3,6,9\}$, $\{1,4,7\}$, $\{2,5,8\}$.
$n(R)=4^2+3^2+3^2=34$, so Statement I is incorrect.
"Same remainder" is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so R is an equivalence relation: Statement II is correct.

questions.text: Consider two sets $A=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}: \left|\left(|x-3|-3\right)\right|\le1\}$ and $B=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}-\{1, 2\}: \dfrac{(x-2)(x-4)}{x-1}\log_e\left(|x-2|\right)=0\right\}$. Then the number of onto functions $f: A\rightarrow B$ is equal to
questions.sol:
A: $2\le|x-3|\le4$, so $x-3\in\{-4,-3,-2,2,3,4\}$ and $A=\{-1,0,1,5,6,7\}$ (6 elements).
B: $x=4$ (from $x-4=0$) or $|x-2|=1$, i.e. $x=3$ ($x=1$ and $x=2$ are excluded). So $B=\{3,4\}$.
Onto functions from a 6-element set to a 2-element set: $2^6-2=62$.

questions.text: The sum of all the real solutions of the equation $\log_{(x+3)}\left(6x^2+28x+30\right)=5-2\log_{(6x+10)}\left(x^2+6x+9\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$6x^2+28x+30=(x+3)(6x+10)$ and $x^2+6x+9=(x+3)^2$. Put $t=\log_{(x+3)}(6x+10)$.
The equation becomes $1+t=5-\dfrac4t$, i.e. $(t-2)^2=0$, so $t=2$ and $6x+10=(x+3)^2$, i.e. $x^2=1$.
Both $x=1$ (bases 4 and 16) and $x=-1$ (bases 2 and 4) are valid. Sum $=0$.

questions.text: If $z=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}+\dfrac i2$, $i=\sqrt{-1}$, then $\left(z^{201}-i\right)^8$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$z=\cos\dfrac\pi6+i\sin\dfrac\pi6$, so $z^{201}=\cos\dfrac{201\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{201\pi}{6}$.
$\dfrac{201\pi}{6}=32\pi+\dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, so $z^{201}=-i$.
$\left(z^{201}-i\right)^8=(-2i)^8=256$.

questions.text:
The system of linear equations
$x+y+z=6$
$2x+5y+az=36$
$x+2y+3z=b$
has
questions.sol:
$\Delta=\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\2&5&a\\1&2&3\end{vmatrix}=8-a$, so for $a=8$ there is no unique solution.
With $a=8$: $2x+5y+8z=-1(x+y+z)+3(x+2y+3z)$ on the left, so the system is consistent only if $36=-6+3b$, i.e. $b=14$.
So $a=8$, $b=14$ gives infinitely many solutions.

questions.text: Let $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}a_k=\alpha n^2+\beta n$. If $a_{10}=59$ and $a_6=7a_1$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$a_k=S_k-S_{k-1}=\alpha(2k-1)+\beta$.
$a_{10}=19\alpha+\beta=59$ and $a_6=11\alpha+\beta=7(\alpha+\beta)$, so $4\alpha=6\beta$.
Then $\beta=\dfrac{2\alpha}{3}$, $\dfrac{59\alpha}{3}=59$, $\alpha=3$, $\beta=2$, and $\alpha+\beta=5$.

questions.text: The number of ways, in which 16 oranges can be distributed to four children such that each child gets at least one orange, is
questions.sol:
Identical oranges, each child at least one: the number of positive integer solutions of $x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4=16$.
$\binom{15}{3}=455$.

questions.text: Bag A contains 9 white and 8 black balls, while bag B contains 6 white and 4 black balls. One ball is randomly picked up from the bag B and mixed up with the balls in the bag A. Then a ball is randomly drawn from the bag A. If the probability, that the ball drawn is white, is $\dfrac pq$, $\gcd(p, q)=1$, then $p+q$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Bag A then has 18 balls.
$P(\text{white})=\dfrac{6}{10}\cdot\dfrac{10}{18}+\dfrac{4}{10}\cdot\dfrac{9}{18}=\dfrac{60+36}{180}=\dfrac{8}{15}$.
$p+q=23$.

questions.text:
If the mean and the variance of the data
Class4$-$88$-$1212$-$1616$-$20
Frequency3$\lambda$47
are $\mu$ and 19 respectively, then the value of $\lambda+\mu$ is
questions.sol:
Class marks 6, 10, 14, 18. $N=14+\lambda$, $\sum fx=200+10\lambda$, $\sum fx^2=3160+100\lambda$.
Try $\lambda=6$: $N=20$, mean $=13$, variance $=\dfrac{3760}{20}-169=19$. This fits (and the variance condition gives a quadratic in $\lambda$ whose other root is not a whole number).
So $\lambda=6$, $\mu=13$, $\lambda+\mu=19$.

questions.text: If the points of intersection of the ellipses $x^2+2y^2-6x-12y+23=0$ and $4x^2+2y^2-20x-12y+35=0$ lie on a circle of radius $r$ and centre $(a, b)$, then the value of $ab+18r^2$ is
questions.sol:
Curves through the common points: $E_1+kE_2=0$. Equal coefficients of $x^2$ and $y^2$: $1+4k=2+2k$, so $k=\dfrac12$.
$E_1+\dfrac12E_2$: $3x^2+3y^2-16x-18y+\dfrac{81}{2}=0$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-\dfrac{16}{3}x-6y+\dfrac{27}{2}=0$.
Centre $\left(\dfrac83,3\right)$, $r^2=\dfrac{64}{9}+9-\dfrac{27}{2}=\dfrac{47}{18}$.
$ab+18r^2=8+47=55$.

questions.text: An equilateral triangle OAB is inscribed in the parabola $y^2=4x$ with the vertex O at the vertex of the parabola. Then the minimum distance of the circle having AB as a diameter from the origin is
questions.sol:
By symmetry A and B are $(t^2,\pm2t)$, and OA makes $30^\circ$ with the axis: $\dfrac{2t}{t^2}=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$, so $t=2\sqrt3$.
$A=(12,4\sqrt3)$, $B=(12,-4\sqrt3)$. The circle on AB has centre $(12,0)$ and radius $4\sqrt3$.
Minimum distance from O $=12-4\sqrt3=4\left(3-\sqrt3\right)$.

questions.text: Let PQ be a chord of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{4}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, perpendicular to the x-axis such that OPQ is an equilateral triangle, O being the centre of the hyperbola. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is $\sqrt3$, then the area of the triangle OPQ is
questions.sol:
$b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=4\times2=8$.
Let $P=(h,k)$, $Q=(h,-k)$. Equilateral with O: $k=h\tan30^\circ=\dfrac h{\sqrt3}$.
$\dfrac{h^2}{4}-\dfrac{h^2}{24}=1 \Rightarrow h^2=\dfrac{24}{5}$.
Area $=hk=\dfrac{h^2}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{24}{5\sqrt3}=\dfrac{8\sqrt3}{5}$.

questions.text: Let $A(1, 2)$ and $C(-3, -6)$ be two diagonally opposite vertices of a rhombus, whose sides AD and BC are parallel to the line $7x-y=14$. If $B(\alpha, \beta)$ and $D(\gamma, \delta)$ are the other two vertices, then $|\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta|$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Diagonals bisect each other at right angles at $M(-1,-2)$. AC has slope 2, so BD has slope $-\dfrac12$: $x+2y+5=0$.
AD has slope 7 through A: $y-2=7(x-1)$. Meeting BD: $D=\left(\dfrac13,-\dfrac83\right)$, and $B=2M-D=\left(-\dfrac73,-\dfrac43\right)$.
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=-\dfrac73-\dfrac43+\dfrac13-\dfrac83=-6$, so the answer is 6.

questions.text: Let $\dfrac\pi2<\theta<\pi$ and $\cot\theta=-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt2}$. Then the value of $\sin\left(\dfrac{15\theta}{2}\right)\left(\cos8\theta+\sin8\theta\right)+\cos\left(\dfrac{15\theta}{2}\right)\left(\cos8\theta-\sin8\theta\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Regroup: $\left[\sin\dfrac{15\theta}{2}\cos8\theta-\cos\dfrac{15\theta}{2}\sin8\theta\right]+\left[\cos\dfrac{15\theta}{2}\cos8\theta+\sin\dfrac{15\theta}{2}\sin8\theta\right]=\sin\left(-\dfrac\theta2\right)+\cos\dfrac\theta2$.
So the value is $\cos\dfrac\theta2-\sin\dfrac\theta2$, which is negative since $\dfrac\pi4<\dfrac\theta2<\dfrac\pi2$; its square is $1-\sin\theta$.
$\csc^2\theta=1+\dfrac18$, so $\sin\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt2}{3}$ and $1-\sin\theta=\dfrac{(\sqrt2-1)^2}{3}$.
Value $=-\dfrac{\sqrt2-1}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{1-\sqrt2}{\sqrt3}$.

questions.text: Let $\vec a=\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec b=2\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$, $\vec c=\lambda\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec v=\vec a\times\vec b$. If $\vec v\cdot\vec c=11$ and the length of the projection of $\vec b$ on $\vec c$ is $p$, then $9p^2$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\vec v=\vec a\times\vec b=(-1,7,5)$, so $\vec v\cdot\vec c=-\lambda+12=11$ and $\lambda=1$.
$p=\dfrac{\vec b\cdot\vec c}{|\vec c|}=\dfrac{2+1-1}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}$.
$9p^2=9\times\dfrac43=12$.

questions.text: Let $\vec a, \vec b, \vec c$ be three vectors such that $\vec a\times\vec b=2\left(\vec a\times\vec c\right)$. If $|\vec a|=1$, $\left|\vec b\right|=4$, $|\vec c|=2$, and the angle between $\vec b$ and $\vec c$ is $60^\circ$, then $\left|\vec a\cdot\vec c\right|$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\vec a\times\left(\vec b-2\vec c\right)=\vec0$, so $\vec b-2\vec c=t\vec a$ for some $t$.
$\vec b\cdot\vec c=4\times2\times\dfrac12=4$. $\left|\vec b-2\vec c\right|^2=16+16-16=16$, so $|t|=4$.
Dot $\vec b=2\vec c+t\vec a$ with $\vec c$: $4=8+t(\vec a\cdot\vec c)$, so $t(\vec a\cdot\vec c)=-4$ and $\left|\vec a\cdot\vec c\right|=1$.

questions.text:
If $f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{a|x|+x^2-2\left(\sin|x|\right)\left(\cos|x|\right)}{x}, & x\neq0\\ b, & x=0\end{cases}$
is continuous at $x=0$, then $a+b$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The numerator is $a|x|+x^2-\sin2|x|$.
As $x\to0^+$: $\dfrac{ax+x^2-\sin2x}{x}\to a-2$. As $x\to0^-$ ($|x|=-x$): $\dfrac{-ax+x^2+\sin2x}{x}\to-a+2$.
Continuity needs $a-2=2-a=b$, so $a=2$, $b=0$ and $a+b=2$.

questions.text: The least value of $\left(\cos^2\theta-6\sin\theta\cos\theta+3\sin^2\theta+2\right)$ is
questions.sol:
$\cos^2\theta+3\sin^2\theta=1+2\sin^2\theta=2-\cos2\theta$ and $6\sin\theta\cos\theta=3\sin2\theta$.
Expression $=4-\left(\cos2\theta+3\sin2\theta\right)$, and $\cos2\theta+3\sin2\theta$ is at most $\sqrt{10}$.
Least value $=4-\sqrt{10}$.

questions.text: Let $I(x)=\displaystyle\int\frac{3\,dx}{(4x+6)\left(\sqrt{4x^2+8x+3}\right)}$ and $I(0)=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}+20$. If $I\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac{a\sqrt2}{b}+c$, where $a, b, c\in\mathbb{N}$, $\gcd(a, b)=1$, then $a+b+c$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Put $u=2x+2$: $4x^2+8x+3=u^2-1$, $4x+6=2(u+1)$, $dx=\dfrac{du}2$, so $I=\dfrac34\displaystyle\int\frac{du}{(u+1)\sqrt{u^2-1}}$.
Since $\dfrac{d}{du}\sqrt{\dfrac{u-1}{u+1}}=\dfrac{1}{(u+1)\sqrt{u^2-1}}$, $I=\dfrac34\sqrt{\dfrac{2x+1}{2x+3}}+C$.
$I(0)=\dfrac34\cdot\dfrac1{\sqrt3}+C=\dfrac{\sqrt3}4+C$, so $C=20$.
$I\left(\dfrac12\right)=\dfrac34\cdot\dfrac1{\sqrt2}+20=\dfrac{3\sqrt2}{8}+20$: $a+b+c=3+8+20=31$.

questions.text: The area of the region enclosed between the circles $x^2+y^2=4$ and $x^2+(y-2)^2=4$ is:
questions.sol:
Both radii are 2 and the centres are 2 apart; the circles meet where $y=1$, $x=\pm\sqrt3$.
Each circle contributes a segment cut off by the chord $y=1$, with central angle $\dfrac{2\pi}3$: area $\dfrac12\cdot4\left(\dfrac{2\pi}3-\sin\dfrac{2\pi}3\right)=\dfrac{4\pi}3-\sqrt3$.
Total $=2\left(\dfrac{4\pi}3-\sqrt3\right)=\dfrac23\left(4\pi-3\sqrt3\right)$.

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}0&2&-3\\-2&0&1\\3&-1&0\end{bmatrix}$ and B be a matrix such that $B(I-A)=I+A$. Then the sum of the diagonal elements of $B^TB$ is equal to ____
questions.sol:
$A^T=-A$ (A is skew-symmetric), and $I-A$ is invertible, so $B=(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}$.
$B^T=\left((I-A)^{-1}\right)^T(I-A)=(I+A)^{-1}(I-A)$.
$I+A$ and $I-A$ commute, so $B^TB=(I+A)^{-1}(I-A)(I+A)(I-A)^{-1}=I$.
Trace of $B^TB=3$.

questions.text: Let S denote the set of 4-digit numbers $abcd$ such that $a>b>c>d$ and P denote the set of 5-digit numbers having product of its digits equal to 20. Then $n(S)+n(P)$ is equal to ____
questions.sol:
S: any 4 different digits from 0-9 arranged in decreasing order (the first digit is then never 0): $\binom{10}{4}=210$.
P: $20=2^2\times5$ with digits from $\{1,2,4,5\}$: $\{5,4,1,1,1\}$ gives $\dfrac{5!}{3!}=20$; $\{5,2,2,1,1\}$ gives $\dfrac{5!}{2!2!}=30$. So $n(P)=50$.
$n(S)+n(P)=260$.

questions.text: If the image of the point $P(a, 2, a)$ in the line $\dfrac x2=\dfrac{y+a}{1}=\dfrac z1$ is Q and the image of Q in the line $\dfrac{x-2b}{2}=\dfrac{y-a}{1}=\dfrac{z+2b}{-5}$ is P, then $a+b$ is equal to ____.
questions.sol:
The midpoint M of PQ is the foot of the perpendicular on both lines, so M is their common point, and PQ is perpendicular to both directions $(2,1,1)$ and $(2,1,-5)$, i.e. parallel to $(-1,2,0)$.
Common point: $(2s,-a+s,s)=(2b+2t,a+t,-2b-5t)$ gives $b=2a$ and $M=(2a,0,a)$.
$\overrightarrow{MP}=(-a,2,0)$ must be parallel to $(-1,2,0)$, so $a=1$, $b=2$, and $a+b=3$.

questions.text: The number of elements in the set $S=\left\{x: x\in[0, 100]\text{ and }\displaystyle\int_0^xt^2\sin(x-t)\,dt=x^2\right\}$ is ____
questions.sol:
Substitute $t\to x-t$: $\displaystyle\int_0^x(x-t)^2\sin t\,dt$. Integrating by parts twice gives $x^2-2+2\cos x$.
So $x^2-2+2\cos x=x^2$, i.e. $\cos x=1$, $x=2k\pi$.
In $[0,100]$: $k=0,1,\ldots,15$ ($15\times2\pi\approx94.2$, $16\times2\pi\approx100.5$). Number of elements $=16$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the solution curve $y=f(x)$ of the differential equation $\left(x^2-4\right)y'-2xy+2x\left(4-x^2\right)^2=0$, $x>2$, passes through the point $(3, 15)$, then the local maximum value of $f$ is______
questions.sol:
Divide by $x^2-4$: $y'-\dfrac{2x}{x^2-4}y=-2x\left(x^2-4\right)$. The integrating factor is $\dfrac1{x^2-4}$.
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{x^2-4}\right)=-2x$, so $\dfrac{y}{x^2-4}=-x^2+C$. At $(3,15)$: $3=-9+C$, $C=12$.
$f(x)=\left(x^2-4\right)\left(12-x^2\right)$; with $u=x^2$ this is largest at $u=8$ ($x=2\sqrt2>2$).
Local maximum value $=4\times4=16$.

questions.text: To compare EMF of two cells using potentiometer the balancing lengths obtained are 200 cm and 150 cm. The least count of scale is 1 cm. The percentage error in the ratio of EMFs is ________
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. The working gives about 1.17%, which is not one of the options.
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{E_1}{E_2}=\dfrac{l_1}{l_2}$, so the percentage error is $\left(\dfrac{1}{200}+\dfrac{1}{150}\right)\times100\approx1.17\%$.
This is not among the options.

questions.text:
A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after 2 s of free fall and starts deaccelerating with 3 m/s$^2$. At 10 m height from ground, while descending with the help of parachute, the speed of paratrooper is 5 m/s. The initial height of the airplane is _______m.
$(g=10\text{ m/s}^2)$
questions.sol:
Free fall for 2 s: falls $\dfrac12\times10\times2^2=20$ m and reaches 20 m/s.
Slowing at 3 m/s$^2$ from 20 m/s to 5 m/s: distance $=\dfrac{20^2-5^2}{2\times3}=62.5$ m.
Initial height $=20+62.5+10=92.5$ m.

questions.text: A bead $P$ sliding on a frictionless semi-circular string $(ACB)$ and it is at point $S$ at $t=0$ and at this instant the horizontal component of its velocity is $v$. Another bead $Q$ of the same mass as $P$ is ejected from point $A$ at $t=0$ along the horizontal string $AB$, with the speed $v$, friction between the beads and the respective strings may be neglected in both cases. Let $t_P$ and $t_Q$ be the respective times taken by beads $P$ and $Q$ to reach the point $B$, then the relation between $t_P$ and $t_Q$ is
questions.sol:
Q moves at constant speed $v$ over $AB=2R$: $t_Q=\dfrac{2R}{v}$.
At S the tangent is at $45^\circ$, so P's speed there is $\sqrt2v$, and it falls further to C before rising to B, which speeds it up over most of the path.
P only has the arc from S to B, $\dfrac{3\pi R}{4}\approx2.36R$, to cover at a speed of about $\sqrt2v$ or more: about $\dfrac{1.67R}{v}$, less than $\dfrac{2R}v$. So $t_P<t_Q$.

questions.text:
A block is sliding down on an inclined plane of slope $\theta$ and at an instant $t=0$ this block is given an upward momentum so that it starts moving up on the inclined surface with velocity $u$. The distance $(S)$ travelled by the block before its velocity become zero, is ________.
($g=$ gravitational acceleration)
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. The question gives no information about friction, so the distance cannot be fixed from the data given.
questions.sol:
If the block slides down at constant speed, friction balances the component of gravity: $\mu g\cos\theta=g\sin\theta$. Moving up, the retardation is then $2g\sin\theta$ and $S=\dfrac{u^2}{4g\sin\theta}$.
On a smooth incline it would be $\dfrac{u^2}{2g\sin\theta}$. The question does not say which, which is why it was dropped.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio $2:2:3$. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of 18 m/s each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is ___ m/s.
questions.sol:
Masses: 4 kg, 4 kg and 6 kg.
The two 4 kg pieces have perpendicular momenta of $72$ kg m/s each; their resultant is $72\sqrt2$ kg m/s.
The total momentum stays zero, so $6v=72\sqrt2$ and $v=12\sqrt2$ m/s.

questions.text:
A small metallic sphere of diameter 2 mm and density 10.5 g/cm$^3$ is dropped in glycerine having viscosity 10 Poise and density 1.5 g/cm$^3$ respectively. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is ____ cm/s.
$\left(\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\text{ and }g=10\text{ m/s}^2\right)$
questions.sol:
$v_t=\dfrac{2r^2(\rho-\sigma)g}{9\eta}$ with $r=10^{-3}$ m, $\rho-\sigma=9000$ kg/m$^3$, $\eta=1$ Pa s.
$v_t=\dfrac{2\times10^{-6}\times9000\times10}{9}=0.02$ m/s $=2.0$ cm/s.

questions.text:
An air bubble of volume 2.9 cm$^3$ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of 5 m deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is 17 $^\circ$C. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is 27 $^\circ$C, is ____ cm$^3$.
($g=10$ m/s$^2$, density of water $=10^3$ kg/m$^3$, and 1 atm pressure is $10^5$ Pa)
questions.sol:
Pressure at the bottom $=10^5+10^3\times10\times5=1.5\times10^5$ Pa; at the surface $10^5$ Pa.
$\dfrac{P_1V_1}{T_1}=\dfrac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$: $V_2=2.9\times1.5\times\dfrac{300}{290}=4.5$ cm$^3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
One mole of an ideal diatomic gas expands from volume $V$ to $2V$ isothermally at a temperature 27 $^\circ$C and does $W$ joule of work. If the gas undergoes same magnitude of expansion adiabatically from 27 $^\circ$C doing the same amount of work $W$, then its final temperature will be (close to) _________$^\circ$C.
$(\log_e2=0.693)$
questions.sol:
Isothermal: $W=RT\ln2=8.314\times300\times0.693\approx1728$ J.
Adiabatic work comes from internal energy: $W=\dfrac52R(300-T)$, so $300-T=\dfrac{1728}{2.5\times8.314}\approx83$ K.
$T\approx217$ K $\approx-56\ ^\circ$C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The internal energy of a monoatomic gas is 3nRT. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of 17 cm$^2$ and fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by suppling 126 J heat. If the temperature rises by 4 $^\circ$C, then the piston will move ________ cm.
(atmospheric pressure $=10^5$ Pa)
questions.sol:
Using the given internal energy, $\Delta U=3R\Delta T=3\times8.3\times4\approx99.6$ J.
Work done against the atmosphere $=Q-\Delta U\approx126-99.6=26.4$ J $=P\,A\,x$.
$x=\dfrac{26.4}{10^5\times17\times10^{-4}}\approx0.155$ m $=15.5$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 5 mm is charged by a battery. On introducing a mica sheet of 2 mm and maintaining the connections of the plates with the terminals of the battery, it is found that it draws 25% more charge from the battery. The dielectric constant of mica is _________.
questions.sol:
At fixed voltage the charge is proportional to capacitance, so $C'=1.25C$.
$\dfrac{C'}{C}=\dfrac{5}{3+\frac2K}=1.25 \Rightarrow 3+\dfrac2K=4 \Rightarrow K=2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Suppose a long solenoid of 100 cm length, radius 2 cm having 500 turns per unit length, carries a current $I=10\sin(\omega t)$ A, where $\omega=1000$ rad./s. A circular conducting loop $(B)$ of radius 1 cm coaxially slided through the solenoid at a speed $v=1$ cm/s. The r.m.s. current through the loop when the coil $B$ is inserted 10 cm inside the solenoid is $\alpha/\sqrt2$ $\mu$A. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
[Resistance of the loop $=10\ \Omega$]
questions.sol:
Inside the solenoid the field is uniform, so only the changing current induces an EMF: $\Phi=\mu_0nI\pi r^2$.
Peak EMF $=\mu_0n\pi r^2I_0\omega=4\pi\times10^{-7}\times500\times\pi\times10^{-4}\times10\times1000\approx1.97\times10^{-3}$ V (taking $n=500$ per metre).
Peak current $=\dfrac{1.97\times10^{-3}}{10}\approx197\ \mu$A, so the r.m.s. current is $\dfrac{197}{\sqrt2}\ \mu$A and $\alpha=197$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The current passing through a conducting loop in the form of equilateral triangle of side $4\sqrt3$ cm is 2 A. The magnetic field at its centroid is $\alpha\times10^{-5}$ T. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
(Given : $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}$ SI units)
questions.sol:
Distance of the centroid from each side: $d=\dfrac{a}{2\sqrt3}=2$ cm.
Each side: $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{4\pi d}(\sin60^\circ+\sin60^\circ)=\dfrac{10^{-7}\times2}{0.02}\times\sqrt3=\sqrt3\times10^{-5}$ T.
Three sides add: $3\sqrt3\times10^{-5}$ T, so $\alpha=3\sqrt3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Two shorts dipoles $(A, B)$, $A$ having charges $\pm2\ \mu$C and length 1 cm and $B$ having charges $\pm4\ \mu$C and length 1 cm are placed with their centres 80 cm apart as shown in the figure. The electric field at a point P, equi-distant from the centres of both dipoles is _________N/C.
questions.sol:
P is 40 cm from each centre: on the axis of A and on the equatorial line of B.
$p_A=2\times10^{-6}\times0.01=2\times10^{-8}$ C m: $E_A=\dfrac{2kp_A}{r^3}=\dfrac{2\times9\times10^9\times2\times10^{-8}}{0.064}=5625$ N/C.
$p_B=4\times10^{-8}$ C m: $E_B=\dfrac{kp_B}{r^3}=5625$ N/C, at right angles to $E_A$.
$E=5625\sqrt2=\dfrac9{16}\sqrt2\times10^4$ N/C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Two charges 7 $\mu$C and $-2\ \mu$C are placed at $(-9, 0, 0)$ cm and $(9, 0, 0)$ cm respectively in an external field $E=\dfrac{A}{r^2}\hat r$, where $A=9\times10^5$ N/C.m$^2$.
Considering the potential at infinity is 0, the electrostatic energy of the configuration is _______J.
questions.sol:
The external potential is $V=\dfrac Ar$; both charges are at $r=0.09$ m, where $V=10^7$ V.
Energy in the external field: $7\times10^{-6}\times10^7-2\times10^{-6}\times10^7=70-20=50$ J.
Mutual energy: $\dfrac{9\times10^9\times7\times10^{-6}\times(-2\times10^{-6})}{0.18}=-0.7$ J.
Total $=49.3$ J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A circular loop of radius 7 cm is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.2 T directed perpendicular to plane of loop. The loop is converted into a square loop in 0.5 s. The EMF induced in the loop is________ mV.
questions.sol:
Wire length $=2\pi\times7=44$ cm, so the square has side 11 cm.
Change in area $=154-121=33$ cm$^2=33\times10^{-4}$ m$^2$.
$\varepsilon=\dfrac{B\Delta A}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{0.2\times33\times10^{-4}}{0.5}=1.32\times10^{-3}$ V $=1.32$ mV.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant $k=3$ and permeability of $\mu=2\mu_0$, is
($\mu_0=$ permeability of vacuum)
questions.sol:
$v=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\mu\varepsilon}}=\dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r\varepsilon_r}}$.
$\dfrac cv=\sqrt{2\times3}=\sqrt6$, so the ratio is $\sqrt6:1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
When an unpolarized light falls at a particular angle on a glass plate (placed in air), it is observed that the reflected beam is linearly polarized. The angle of refracted beam with respect to the normal is_______.
($\tan^{-1}(1.52)=57.7^\circ$, refractive indices of air and glass are 1.00 and 1.52, respectively.)
questions.sol:
The reflected light is fully polarised at Brewster's angle, $i_B=\tan^{-1}(1.52)=57.7^\circ$.
At this angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, so $r=90^\circ-57.7^\circ=32.3^\circ$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A prism of angle $75^\circ$ and refractive index $\sqrt3$ is coated with thin film of refractive index 1.5 only at the back exit surface. To have total internal reflection at the back exit surface the incident angle must be_______.
($\sin15^\circ=0.25$ and $\sin25^\circ=0.43$)
questions.note: Official final key: options (1), (3) and (4) are all accepted. The working gives an angle of incidence less than about $25^\circ$, and all three of these satisfy that.
questions.sol:
Critical angle at the prism-film surface: $\sin C=\dfrac{1.5}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, $C=60^\circ$.
TIR needs $r_2\ge60^\circ$, so $r_1=75^\circ-r_2\le15^\circ$.
$\sin i=\sqrt3\sin r_1\le\sqrt3\times0.25\approx0.43=\sin25^\circ$, so $i$ must be less than about $25^\circ$.
Options (1), (3) and (4) all satisfy this.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following pair of nuclei are isobars of the element?
questions.sol:
Isobars have the same mass number A but different atomic numbers.
${}^3_1\mathrm{H}$ and ${}^3_2\mathrm{He}$ both have $A=3$. (The H and U pairs are isotopes; Hg-198 and Au-197 have the same number of neutrons, 118, so they are isotones.)
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: For the given logic gate circuit, which of the following is the correct truth table ?
questions.sol:
The OR gate gives $n+m$; the NAND gate takes $n$ and $n+m$.
$z=\overline{n\cdot(n+m)}=\overline{n}$, since $n(n+m)=n$.
So $z=1$ when $n=0$ and $z=0$ when $n=1$: table (3).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Suppose there is a uniform circular disc of mass $M$ kg and radius $r$ m shown in figure. The shaded regions are cut out from the disc. The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis $A$ of the disc is given by $\dfrac{x}{256}Mr^2$. The value of $x$ is_______.
questions.sol:
Each hole has radius $\dfrac r4$, so its mass is $\dfrac{M}{16}$; its centre is $\dfrac{3r}{4}$ from the axis (the $135^\circ$ angle does not matter).
Each hole about A: $\dfrac M{16}\left(\dfrac{r^2}{32}+\dfrac{9r^2}{16}\right)=\dfrac{19Mr^2}{512}$.
$I=\dfrac{Mr^2}{2}-2\times\dfrac{19Mr^2}{512}=\dfrac{128-19}{256}Mr^2=\dfrac{109}{256}Mr^2$, so $x=109$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: A ball of radius $r$ and density $\rho$ dropped through a viscous liquid of density $\sigma$ and viscosity $\eta$ attains its terminal velocity at time $t$, given by $t=A\rho^ar^b\eta^c\sigma^d$, where $A$ is a constant and $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are integers. The value of $\dfrac{b+c}{a+d}$ is _____.
questions.sol:
The speed approaches its terminal value over the time scale $t=\dfrac{m}{6\pi\eta r}=\dfrac{\frac43\pi r^3\rho}{6\pi\eta r}=\dfrac{2r^2\rho}{9\eta}$.
So $a=1$, $b=2$, $c=-1$, $d=0$ (dimensions agree: $\dfrac{\text{kg m}^{-3}\,\text{m}^2}{\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}}=\text{s}$).
$\dfrac{b+c}{a+d}=\dfrac11=1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The velocity of sound in air is doubled when the temperature is raised from 0 $^\circ$C to $\alpha$ $^\circ$C. The value of $\alpha$ is ________.
questions.sol:
$v\propto\sqrt T$, so doubling $v$ needs $4T$: $4\times273=1092$ K.
$\alpha=1092-273=819\ ^\circ$C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The size of the images of an object, formed by a thin lens are equal when the object is placed at two different positions 8 cm and 24 cm from the lens. The focal length of the lens is ________ cm.
questions.sol:
Equal sizes at two object distances needs a convex lens giving one virtual and one real image of the same magnification.
$|m|=\left|\dfrac{f}{f-u}\right|$ (distances as magnitudes): $\dfrac{f}{f-8}=\dfrac{f}{24-f}$, so $f-8=24-f$ and $f=16$ cm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The average energy released per fission for the nucleus of ${}^{235}_{92}\mathrm{U}$ is 190 MeV. When all the atoms of 47 g pure ${}^{235}_{92}\mathrm{U}$ undergo fission process, the energy released is $\alpha\times10^{23}$ MeV. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
(Avogadro Number $=6\times10^{23}$ per mole)
questions.sol:
Number of nuclei $=\dfrac{47}{235}\times6\times10^{23}=1.2\times10^{23}$.
Energy $=1.2\times10^{23}\times190=228\times10^{23}$ MeV, so $\alpha=228$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The work functions of two metals ($\mathrm{M_A}$ and $\mathrm{M_B}$) are in the 1 : 2 ratio. When these metals are exposed to photons of energy 6 eV, the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of $\mathrm{M_A}:\mathrm{M_B}$ is in the ratio of 2.642 : 1. The work functions (in eV) of $\mathrm{M_A}$ and $\mathrm{M_B}$ are respectively.
questions.sol:
Let the work functions be $\phi$ and $2\phi$: $\dfrac{6-\phi}{6-2\phi}=2.642$.
$6-\phi=15.852-5.284\phi \Rightarrow 4.284\phi=9.852 \Rightarrow \phi\approx2.3$ eV.
Work functions: 2.3 eV and 4.6 eV.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Identify the INCORRECT statements from the following:
A. Notation ${}^{24}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$ represents 24 protons and 12 neutrons.
B. Wavelength of a radiation of frequency $4.5\times10^{15}$ s$^{-1}$ is $6.7\times10^{-8}$ m.
C. One radiation has wavelength $=\lambda_1$ (900 nm) and energy $=E_1$. Other radiation has wavelength $=\lambda_2$ (300 nm) and energy $=E_2$. $E_1:E_2=3:1$.
D. Number of photons of light of wavelength 2000 pm that provides 1 J of energy is $1.006\times10^{16}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: ${}^{24}_{12}\mathrm{Mg}$ has 12 protons and 12 neutrons: incorrect.
B: $\lambda=\dfrac{3\times10^8}{4.5\times10^{15}}=6.7\times10^{-8}$ m: correct.
C: $E\propto\dfrac1\lambda$, so $E_1:E_2=300:900=1:3$: incorrect.
D: $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=\dfrac{6.626\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{2\times10^{-9}}=9.94\times10^{-17}$ J, so 1 J needs $1.006\times10^{16}$ photons: correct.
Incorrect: A and C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Which statements are NOT TRUE about $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$?
A. It has a see-saw shape.
B. Xe has 5 electron pairs in its valence shell in $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$.
C. The O$-$Xe$-$O bond angle is close to $180^\circ$.
D. The F$-$Xe$-$F bond angle is close to $180^\circ$.
E. Xe has 16 valence electrons in $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Xe has 4 $\sigma$ bonds and 1 lone pair: trigonal bipyramidal arrangement, see-saw shape (A true), with F atoms axial (F-Xe-F close to $180^\circ$, D true) and O atoms equatorial (O-Xe-O about $105^\circ$, C not true).
Counting the two Xe=O double bonds, Xe has 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 7 electron pairs, i.e. 14 electrons, around it, so B (5 pairs) and E (16 electrons) are not true.
NOT TRUE: B, C and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
It is noticed that $\mathrm{Pb^{2+}}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{Pb^{4+}}$ but $\mathrm{Sn^{2+}}$ is less stable than $\mathrm{Sn^{4+}}$.
Observe the following reactions.
$\mathrm{PbO_2+Pb\rightarrow2PbO}$; $\Delta_rG^\circ(1)$
$\mathrm{SnO_2+Sn\rightarrow2SnO}$; $\Delta_rG^\circ(2)$
Identify the correct set from the following
questions.sol:
Reaction 1 turns Pb(IV) and Pb(0) into the more stable Pb(II), so it is spontaneous: $\Delta_rG^\circ(1)<0$ (inert pair effect).
Reaction 2 turns Sn(IV), the more stable state of tin, into Sn(II), so it is not spontaneous: $\Delta_rG^\circ(2)>0$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the above electrochemical cell where a metal electrode (M) is undergoing redox reaction by forming $\mathrm{M^+}$ $\left(\mathrm{M\rightarrow M^++e^-}\right)$. The cation $\mathrm{M^+}$ is present in two different concentrations $c_1$ and $c_2$ as shown above. Which of the following statement is correct for generating a positive cell potential?
options: If $c_1$ is present at cathode, then $c_1<c_2$.
If $c_1$ is present at anode, then $c_1>c_2$.
If $c_1$ is present at cathode, then $c_1>c_2$.
If $c_1$ is present at anode, then $c_1=c_2$.
questions.sol:
This is a concentration cell: $E_{\text{cell}}=\dfrac{0.059}{1}\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{M^+}]_{\text{cathode}}}{[\mathrm{M^+}]_{\text{anode}}}$.
$E_{\text{cell}}>0$ needs the larger concentration at the cathode.
So if $c_1$ is at the cathode, $c_1>c_2$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given above is the concentration vs time plot for a dissociation reaction : $\mathrm{A\rightarrow nB}$.
Based on the data of the initial phase of the reaction (initial 10 min), the value of n is _____.
questions.sol:
In the first 10 min, [A] falls from 0.05 M to 0.04 M (a change of 0.01 M) while [B] rises from 0 to 0.03 M.
$n=\dfrac{0.03}{0.01}=3$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Observe the following reactions at T(K).
I. A $\rightarrow$ products.
II. $\mathrm{5Br^-(aq)+BrO_3^-(aq)+6H^+(aq)\rightarrow3Br_2(aq)+3H_2O(\mathit{l})}$
Both the reactions are started at 10.00 am. The rates of these reactions at 10.10 am are same. The value of $-\dfrac{\Delta[\mathrm{Br^-}]}{\Delta t}$ at 10.10 am is $2\times10^{-4}$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$. The concentration of A at 10.10 am is $10^{-2}$ mol L$^{-1}$. What is the first order rate constant (in min$^{-1}$) of reaction I?
questions.sol:
Rate of reaction II $=-\dfrac15\dfrac{\Delta[\mathrm{Br^-}]}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{2\times10^{-4}}{5}=4\times10^{-5}$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$.
Reaction I has the same rate: $k[\mathrm{A}]=4\times10^{-5}$, so $k=\dfrac{4\times10^{-5}}{10^{-2}}=4\times10^{-3}$ min$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The second ionisation enthalpy of Na is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of Mg.
Statement II: The ionic radius of $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ is larger than that of $\mathrm{F^-}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Removing a second electron from Na means breaking into the noble-gas core ($\mathrm{Na^+}$ is $[\mathrm{Ne}]$), whereas $\mathrm{Mg^+}$ still has a 3s electron: Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{F^-}$ are isoelectronic, and O has the smaller nuclear charge, so $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ is larger: Statement II is true.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of 'X' and phosphorus is higher than that of the difference between phosphorus and 'Y'. 'X' & 'Y' are respectively
questions.sol:
Electronegativities (Pauling): N 3.0, P 2.1, As 2.0, Sb 1.9, Bi 1.9.
For N and As: $|3.0-2.1|=0.9>|2.1-2.0|=0.1$. The other pairs fail: Bi & N gives $0.2<0.9$; As & Bi gives $0.1<0.2$; As & Sb gives $0.1<0.2$.
X = N, Y = As.

questions.text: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed in the reaction between KI and acidified $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ solution is:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}+6I^-+14H^+\rightarrow2Cr^{3+}+3I_2+7H_2O}$.
Dichromate is reduced to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$: oxidation state $+3$.

questions.text:
Identify the CORRECT set of details from the following:
A. $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ : Inner orbital complex; $\mathrm{d^2sp^3}$ hybridized
B. $\mathrm{[MnCl_6]^{3-}}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$ hybridized
C. $\mathrm{[CoF_6]^{3-}}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\mathrm{d^2sp^3}$ hybridized
D. $\mathrm{[FeF_6]^{3-}}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$ hybridized
E. $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ : Inner orbital complex; $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridized
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ with strong-field $\mathrm{NH_3}$, spin-paired, $\mathrm{d^2sp^3}$ (inner): correct.
B: $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ with weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$ (outer): correct.
C: an outer orbital complex uses $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$, not $\mathrm{d^2sp^3}$: incorrect.
D: $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ with $\mathrm{F^-}$, $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$ (outer): correct.
E: $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ is square planar, $\mathrm{dsp^2}$: incorrect.
A, B and D only.

questions.text: In Carius method 0.2425 g of an organic compound gave 0.5253 g silver chloride. The percentage of chlorine in the organic compound is
questions.sol:
Mass of Cl $=\dfrac{35.5}{143.5}\times0.5253=0.12995$ g.
Percentage $=\dfrac{0.12995}{0.2425}\times100\approx53.58\%$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3\overset{\oplus}{C}}$ is more stable than $\mathrm{\overset{\oplus}{C}H_3}$ as nine hyperconjugation interactions are possible in $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3\overset{\oplus}{C}}$.
Statement II: $\mathrm{\overset{\oplus}{C}H_3}$ is less stable than $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3\overset{\oplus}{C}}$ as only three hyperconjugation interactions are possible in $\mathrm{\overset{\oplus}{C}H_3}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
The tert-butyl cation has 9 C-H bonds next to the positive carbon, giving nine hyperconjugation structures, so it is much more stable: Statement I is true.
$\mathrm{CH_3^+}$ has no C-H bond on a neighbouring carbon, so it has no hyperconjugation at all: Statement II is false.

questions.text: Identify (P)
questions.note: Both (1) and (2) are tertiary bromides that can form by a 1,2-hydride shift; the final key gives (2).
questions.sol:
Zn removes the two vicinal Br atoms, giving a cyclopentene with the C=C between the carbons that carried Br.
Adding $\mathrm{H^+}$ gives a secondary carbocation next to a ring carbon bearing an alkyl group; a 1,2-hydride shift makes it tertiary.
With the shift from the methyl-bearing carbon, $\mathrm{Br^-}$ adds there: 1-bromo-3-ethyl-1-methylcyclopentane, structure (2), as in the final key.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are TRUE about Haloform reaction?:
A. Sodium hypochlorite reacts with KI to give KOI.
B. KOI is a reducing agent.
C. $\alpha$, $\beta$-unsaturated methylketone $\left(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-\overset{\underset{\|}{O}}{C}-CH_3}\right)$ will give iodoform reaction.
D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test.
E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A: $\mathrm{NaOCl+KI\rightarrow KOI+NaCl}$: true.
B: KOI (hypoiodite) is an oxidising agent: false.
C: the compound has a $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ group, so it gives iodoform: true.
D: isopropyl alcohol, $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}$, does give the test: false.
E: methanoic acid has no $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$ group: false.
A and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A mixed ether (P), when heated with excess of hot concentrated hydrogen iodide produces two different alkyl iodides which when treated with aq. NaOH give compounds (Q) and (R). Both (Q) and (R) give yellow precipitate with NaOI. Identify the mixed ether (P):
questions.sol:
Excess HI breaks both C-O bonds, giving two alkyl iodides, and aq. NaOH turns them into the two alcohols. Both must give iodoform, so each must be ethanol or have a $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)-}$ group.
(3) is the ether of ethanol and butan-2-ol (ethyl sec-butyl ether), and both alcohols give iodoform.
(1) gives a tertiary alcohol, (2) gives benzyl alcohol and (4) gives 1-phenylpropan-1-ol, none of which gives iodoform.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: [benzene-1,2-diamine, shown in the figure] can be synthesized from [1,2-dipropylbenzene, shown in the figure] using simpler reagents in the order i) Acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$, ii) Ammonia, iii) Bromine and alkali
Statement II: [4-methylaniline] can be converted into [3,5-dibromotoluene] using reagents in the order i) Bromine-$\mathrm{H_2O}$ ii) $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}$ (0 - 5 $^\circ$C) (iii) Aq. $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.note: The final key gives (1), both true, reading step ii) as forming the diamide (phthalamide). If ammonia and heat give phthalimide instead, step iii) gives 2-aminobenzoic acid and Statement I would be false. The answer here follows the final key.
questions.sol:
Statement I: acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ oxidises both side chains, giving benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic (phthalic) acid. Ammonia converts it to the diamide, $\mathrm{C_6H_4(CONH_2)_2}$. Bromine and alkali (Hofmann bromamide reaction) turn each $\mathrm{-CONH_2}$ into $\mathrm{-NH_2}$, giving benzene-1,2-diamine. True.
Statement II: bromine water puts Br at both positions ortho to $\mathrm{NH_2}$ in 4-methylaniline; diazotisation and $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ then replace $\mathrm{-N_2^+}$ by H, leaving Br at positions 3 and 5 of toluene. True.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A student has been given a compound "$x$" of molecular formula- $\mathrm{C_6H_7N}$. '$x$' is sparingly soluble in water. However, on addition of dilute mineral acid, '$x$' becomes soluble in water. '$x$' when treated with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and KOH(alc), '$y$' is produced. '$y$' has a specific unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, '$x$' gives a compound '$z$' which is soluble in alkali. The number of different "H" atoms present in '$z$' is:-
questions.sol:
$x$ is aniline (a primary amine: carbylamine test gives phenyl isocyanide, $y$). With benzenesulphonyl chloride it gives $z$, $\mathrm{C_6H_5SO_2NHC_6H_5}$, soluble in alkali because of the acidic N-H.
Different H atoms in $z$: ortho, meta and para H of each ring (3 + 3) and the N-H (1): 7.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of
questions.sol:
The bases and the phosphate are not chiral.
The chirality comes from the sugar (D-ribose in RNA, D-2-deoxyribose in DNA): the D-sugar component.

questions.text:
Iodoform test can differentiate between
A. Methanol and Ethanol
B. $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$
C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone
D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one
E. Anisole and acetone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The test distinguishes a pair only if exactly one member gives iodoform.
A: ethanol gives it, methanol does not: yes. E: acetone gives it, anisole does not: yes.
B (neither acid), C (cyclohexanone is not a methyl ketone) and D (pentan-3-one is not a methyl ketone): neither member reacts.
A and E only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Total number of unpaired electrons present in the central metal atoms/ions of $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$, $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]}$, $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{[Pt(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ is _______ .
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$: Ni(0), $\mathrm{d^{10}}$: 0. $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$: $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ $\mathrm{d^8}$, tetrahedral with weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$: 2.
$\mathrm{[PtCl_2(NH_3)_2]}$, $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{[Pt(CN)_4]^{2-}}$: $\mathrm{d^8}$ square planar: 0 each.
Total $=2$.

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction of benzene.
In compound (Q), the percentage of oxygen is _______%. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
Friedel-Crafts acylation at the acid chloride: P is $\mathrm{C_6H_5COCH_2CH_2COCH_3}$ (1-phenylpentane-1,4-dione).
Aqueous NaOH and heat cause an intramolecular aldol condensation (the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ of the methyl ketone attacks the C=O next to the ring), giving 3-phenylcyclopent-2-en-1-one, Q, $\mathrm{C_{11}H_{10}O}$ ($M=158$).
% O $=\dfrac{16}{158}\times100\approx10$.

questions.text:
200 cc of $x\times10^{-3}$ M potassium dichromate is required to oxidise 750 cc of 0.6 M Mohr's salt solution in acidic medium.
Here $x=$ ______.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ takes 6 electrons and each $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ gives 1, so mol $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}=6\times$ mol dichromate.
$750\times0.6=6\times200\times x\times10^{-3}$ (in mmol): $450=1.2x$, so $x=375$.

questions.text:
$\mathrm{X_2(g)+Y_2(g)\rightleftharpoons2Z(g)}$
$\mathrm{X_2(g)}$ and $\mathrm{Y_2(g)}$ are added to a 1 L flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at T(K) with the number of moles of $\mathrm{X_2(g)}$, $\mathrm{Y_2(g)}$ and Z(g) being 3, 3 and 9 mol respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this condition of equilibrium, 10 mol of Z(g) is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at T(K). Then the number of moles of Z(g) in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is _____ . (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$K=\dfrac{9^2}{3\times3}=9$.
After adding 10 mol Z (19 mol), some Z goes back: $\mathrm{X_2}=\mathrm{Y_2}=3+y$, $\mathrm{Z}=19-2y$.
$\dfrac{(19-2y)^2}{(3+y)^2}=9 \Rightarrow 19-2y=9+3y \Rightarrow y=2$.
Moles of Z $=15$.

questions.text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At 320 K, the vapour pressure of the solution, containing 3 mol of A and 1 mol of B is 500 mm Hg. At the same temperature, if 1 mol of A is further added to this solution, vapour pressure of the solution increases by 20 mm Hg. Vapour pressure (in mm Hg) of B in pure state is ________. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
$\dfrac34p_A^\circ+\dfrac14p_B^\circ=500$ and $\dfrac45p_A^\circ+\dfrac15p_B^\circ=520$.
From the first, $p_B^\circ=2000-3p_A^\circ$; substituting: $0.2p_A^\circ=120$, so $p_A^\circ=600$.
$p_B^\circ=2000-1800=200$ mm Hg.
